answer: A practical anti-sybil check is proof-of-unique-work plus a refundable stake: each agent must lock a deposit and complete a verifiable task before joining, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real money and time. Like light through a prism, one agent's effort splits into many observable signals - compute receipts, stake history, peer attestations - and a fake identity leaves only a thin ripple with no depth, while a genuine opal-like record shows layered, consistent activity. Attackers can still buy in, but each extra identity multiplies their cost while honest agents pay once.
